title: Member ID Cards and Replacement Cards for Prairie Ridge Members
content:
## Member ID cards — training note

This training note covers when a Medicaid Managed Care Membership ID card is issued, how lost, stolen and damaged cards are replaced, and on which memberships a card can be issued.

### The rule the desk applies

- A physical ID card is mailed on every new enrollment, on a name change, on an eligibility category change and when the assigned primary care provider changes. None of these count toward the replacement limit.
- A card reported lost, stolen or damaged is replaced by mail while the member's count of replacement cards in the last 365 days is below the category's free replacements per 12 months. Once that limit is reached, the replacement is issued as a digital card in the member portal only, recorded as delivered through the member portal.
- An ID card is issued only for a membership whose status is pending, active, renewal due or in reconsideration.
- There is never a fee for any card.
- A temporary proof-of-coverage letter may be offered while a mailed card is in production.

### How the replacement count is taken

The count covers a rolling 365 calendar days ending on the day the request is handled, both ends included. It counts the cards issued on the membership for a lost, stolen or damaged card and sent by mail. Cards mailed for a new enrollment, a name change, a category change or a primary care provider change are not counted, and a digital-only card issued in the member portal is not a mailed replacement.

### Membership status and card issue

| Membership status | Card can be issued |
|---|---|
| Pending | Yes |
| Active | Yes |
| Renewal due | Yes |
| In reconsideration | Yes |
| Suspended | No |
| Terminated | No |

### Questions answered

**A member in a category with 3 free replacements has had 2 mailed lost-card replacements in the last 365 days. How is a third lost card replaced?** The count (2) is below the limit (3), so the replacement is mailed.

**The same member then reports the card stolen. How is it replaced?** The count is now 3, which has reached the limit, so the replacement is a digital card in the member portal only.

**Does a card mailed because the primary care provider changed use up a replacement?** No. Cards issued for a new enrollment, name change, category change or primary care provider change never count toward the limit.

**Is there a charge for a replacement beyond the limit?** No card carries a fee.

**How long does a mailed card take?** It is produced and posted within the category's mail business days, counted Monday to Friday excluding state holidays.

(The figures in these answers are hypothetical illustrations built on the rule above.)
